correctness.rationale: For 0<k<p^a, the remaining binomial coefficient in C(p^a,k)=(p^a/k)C(p^a-1,k-1) is a unit by Lucas, so the valuation is a-v_p(k). Only k=jp^(a-1) can contribute modulo p^4 after cubing, and at these indices C(p^a,k)/p reduces to (-1)^(j-1)/j. The endpoints sum to 2. For p≥5 the full reciprocal-cube sum is zero modulo p, leaving -1/4 times the half sum. Setting m=p-3, that half sum is (B_m((p+1)/2)-B_m(0))/m by Faulhaber's formula. The coefficients are p-integral since all Bernoulli indices are below p-1. The half-argument formula B_m(1/2)=(2^(1-m)-1)B_m and 2^(1-m)=8 mod p give the half sum -2B_m, hence the frozen coefficient B_m/2. Glaisher's classical binomial congruence detects the same Bernoulli zero modulo p. At p=2 the surviving unit sum is 1, and at p=3 it is 2 modulo 3, giving exact valuation 3 at every height. Divisibility by the cube of p^a for a≥2 requires valuation at least six, so only the stated nonexceptional cases are excluded by the frozen modulus.
residual_risks: The recurrence is a bounded cross-check, not evidence of a universal valuation above four at Wolstenholme primes, nor a test of the full primality conjecture.

evidence: Straub gives Y_d(p^r n) ≡ Y_d(p^(r-1)n) mod p^(3r) for d≥2 and p≥5; Y_3 is Franel.

The OEIS comment describes analytic towers that encode all p-adic digits, a potentially broader relevant result. No matching explicit Franel coefficient was verified in a primary passage of that work.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Straub's result already yields f_(p^a) ≡ f_p mod p⁶ for all a≥2. Stabilizing to an unknown residue does not compute its value. A tower that encodes digits could contain an effective formula or exact specialization, but the OEIS description alone does not determine whether it does.

evidence: Known height stability, the central-binomial criterion and prime-direction divisibility mod p³ are separate established facts. The frozen proof evaluates the remaining alternating reciprocal-cube moment from the binomial units and also handles p=2,3 outside Straub's displayed range.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Once the base Bernoulli coefficient is established, the p≥5 extension is already a corollary of prior stronger stability. The Bernoulli evaluation of the Franel residue is not supplied by that stability or by the classical binomial criterion alone; the new-credit scope excludes both prior ingredients.

evidence: Sun's inspected theorem is about weighted sums of f_k for k<p, principally modulo p², not f_p mod p⁴.
Meštrović reviews the binomial criterion modulo p⁴, which is equivalent to vanishing of the Bernoulli coefficient but does not give a Franel residue in the inspected passage.
The matching indexed entry 6ea940ca2aa7 is the frozen result itself. The distinct ac51f85be5c1 search summary concerns signed binomial powers at p^q-1; no full-text comparison was available.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A signed-power valuation on a row ending in base-p digit p-1 is not an identified substitute for the unsigned cubic Franel sum on row p^a. A connection between the binomial and Franel criteria requires evaluation of the latter coefficient.

evidence: A000172 identifies the sum and records Detlefs's 22 March 2013 iff conjecture for a(n)=2 mod n³ and a comment giving the forward prime direction. No inspection identified a table of the uniform valuation or coefficient. The exact index match is the same frozen entry.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: A table of sequence values or the primality conjecture does not establish the signed Bernoulli digit uniformly in p and a, even if one can compute the digit for individual entries.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct result is the explicit Bernoulli coefficient for the Franel residue, its identification with the Wolstenholme exception and the small-prime valuations. The prime-power stability itself is covered by Straub's stronger theorem for p≥5, and the binomial/Bernoulli Wolstenholme criterion is classical. No independent matching statement for the remaining Franel coefficient was established in the strongest available comparisons; this is a bounded judgment, not a claim of historical priority.
residual_risks: The explicit coefficient may occur in the cited Blanco Gómez tower work or in an earlier exact Franel congruence under different notation. Primary text of the tower reference and full text of the distinct generalized-Franel index entry were not verified.

value.rationale: At canonical input indices for a known primality-test conjecture, this is an exact obstruction, not generic height stability: it explains why essentially the entire prime-power problem falls at valuation three and isolates the precise classical irregularity that can make that obstruction vanish. The small-prime valuations cover the boundary not covered by the cited general odd-prime height-stability theorem. This is useful even though the exceptional case requires finer digits.
residual_risks: No claim that the criterion has no composite solutions or that this modulus settles Wolstenholme-prime powers.
